<thought>The spectrum shows a strong M+2 peak at ~33% of the base peak, matching the characteristic 3:1 chlorine isotopic pattern, so chlorine is definitively present. The sizable M+1 peak (~16% of base) corresponds to the natural 13C abundance and indicates carbon is definitely present. No other element shows a distinctive isotopic signature (e.g., bromine’s ~1:1 M:M+2 is absent, sulfur’s M+2 would be only ~4%). Therefore the definitively identifiable elements are carbon and chlorine.</thought>
<final_answer>['C', 'Cl']</final_answer>
